# Surface Map Contract
A product surface is a coherent unit of externally meaningful behaviour with identifiable entrypoints, state, dependencies, outputs, and failure semantics. Prefer behavioural scopes such as `sprint-execute-resume` over directory scopes such as `internal/sprint`. Good size: one primary workflow, a few state authorities, roughly 5-20 primary production files/symbol clusters, relevant tests and immediate dependencies. Risk: critical/high/normal/low; mappers must not report findings.

display.text:
# Review Doctrine
Findings are hypotheses until challenged. Concrete observable failure beats generic concern. Tests are evidence, not truth. Security requires source -> trust transition -> insufficient control -> meaningful consequence. A clean scanner/test result never proves absence. Separate severity from confidence. Record rejected hypotheses that defend important behaviour. Do not report style nits.

display.text:
# Surface Map — map-05-interface-surfaces (CLI / TUI / web interfaces)

Job: independent product-surface discovery from the interface lens. No findings reported in this phase; risk notes are prioritisation rationale only.

## Provenance

- Target: `/home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-go`, frozen commit `f0fcd0c2107a8e8d69e1283f9e8d5e2c6da94025`. All discovery ran against a dedicated pinned clone (`/tmp/opencode/upgo-frozen`, verified `git rev-parse` = `f0fcd0c`). The live working tree is at `ad0be98`; sole delta vs frozen is `internal/sprint/prompt_context.go` (256 KiB → 512 KiB shared prompt budget) — not interface code. Everything below holds at both commits.
- Planning workspace: `/home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-workspace` @ `ab12dc38059c…` (== HEAD). CURRENT-CONTRACT anchors consulted: `system/contracts/surfaces/{cli,api-contracts,accessibility,frontend}.md`.
- Method: 5 parallel bounded `review-worker` discoveries (CLI grammar, TUI, web routes/lifecycle, web security model, interface convergence/divergence) + mapper verification of load-bearing claims (TUI cancel path `internal/tui/app.go:232-269`; `validCommandOrigin` body vs docstring `internal/web/security.go:269-274`; definition-only helpers `security.go:262-267,300-302`; 27-entry operation-kind enum; zero TUI constructions of `sprint-stage`/`sprint-stage-dry-run`/`validate`; no template/JS issuer of web `study-cancel`).
- Baseline: go test / -race / vet / cover all passed at freeze (state.json).

## Interface topology in one paragraph

Three frontends over one app core. `cmd/ultraplan/main.go` injects `TUIRunner`/`WebRunner` function types into `app.Run` (`internal/app/app.go:88-178`, inversion at `surfaces.go:18-20`); nothing in `internal/app` imports the frontends. CLI handlers mostly call product services directly; TUI and web share the `OperationalUseCases` boundary (`dashboardUseCases`) plus `DurableOperationManager` + `repositoryRunUseCases`, with runtime-backed work funnelling through `sharedOperationRunner` (`operation_runner.go:18-169`). One composition root resolves the workspace identically for all three (`discoverWorkspace`, `app.go:287-298`: `--workspace` flag → `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE` → cwd-ancestry marker walk), and one SQLite run-control repository per workspace root backs observation/cancellation everywhere. Divergence lives in grammar (three arg-parsing styles), durability mechanics (CLI accept has empty digest/no dedup alias vs web/TUI fingerprint digests), and capability coverage (web-only sprint create/model list/timeline; CLI-only `code`, diagnostics export, study reset; TUI-only interactive parallelism form).

---

## Candidate surfaces

Grouping proposal: **A CLI shell** (IA1–IA2), **B Web console** (IB1–IB3), **C TUI** (IC1–IC2), **D Cross-interface** (ID1). Overlaps map-01's coarse S10–S12 but splits them into reviewable units.

### IA1 — `cli-dispatch-exit-contract` (domain A)
- Behaviour: argv dispatch of 15 top-level commands (`--help/-h`, `version`, `init-workspace`, `defaults`, `skills`, `config`, `health`, `storage`, `run`, `project`, `sprint`, `study`, `tui`, `serve`, `code`); whole-argv global `--workspace[=]` scan; exit classes 0–8 with stable code strings; three output styles (jsonEnvelope `{schema_version,command,workspace,status,result}`, ad-hoc sprint-family maps, raw structs); help/version text.
- Files: `cmd/ultraplan/main.go`, `internal/app/{app,json_output,status_json,qa_errors}.go`, per-command `*_commands.go` parsers/dispatchers, contract docs `docs/cli-reference.md`.
- Failure semantics: unknown command → exit 2 stderr (`app.go:175-177`); classified causes preserved (`classedError`, `errorCode` `app.go:41-86`).
- Inventory facts for reviewers: error-classification default differs per family (sprint/study/project → 4; run-control → 6); QA cancel/deadline → 8 while sprint cancellation → 7; some sprint CLI paths classify by error-text sniffing (`strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` → 6, `"failed tasks"` → 8, `sprint_commands.go:269,360-364,507`) whereas the operation-runner path pins no text classification (`failedOperation`, `operations.go:751-796`, pinned by `sprint_error_test.go:29-41`); three arg-parser styles coexist (hand loops, stdlib flag, `orderRunArgs` reorder where an unrecognised dash token becomes positional and a valued-flag swallows a following `--flag` as value, `run_commands.go:463-481`); undocumented surface: `tui`, `storage migrate`, `sprint metrics`, `study runs summary`, flow model/variant override flags, prompt `review`/`--explain`, cancel reason whitelist, `--workspace=` form; embedded `skillsMaterialiseHelp` lists 9 stages while workspace layer defines 11 incl. `reconcile` (`skills_commands.go:119-128` vs `workspace/skills.go:41,231-233`).
- Key tests: `app_test.go` (help/version/unknown/classified cause), `run_commands_test.go`, `sprint_commands_test.go` (exit classes, single JSON failure document, stable QA codes), `study_*_commands_test.go`, `serve_commands_test.go`, `code_commands_test.go` (exit 4/5/8 matrix).
- Seams: every runtime-backed command crosses the durable acceptance seam (`beginDurableCLICommand`, counted by source inventory `run_control_inventory_test.go:11-55`); JSON shapes are the automation contract.
- Risk: normal-high — silent breakage class (exit codes/JSON shapes) consumed by scripts and agents.

### IA2 — `run-cli-observation-control` (domain A)
- Behaviour: `run list|show|follow|cancel|diagnostics` against the shared repository: filtered listing (limit default 50, bounds enforced 1..200 downstream `runcontrol/lifecycle.go:197-202`), snapshot render, follow loop (512-event batches, 250 ms backfill / 1 s idle, exits on terminal && cursor ≥ LastSequence, ctx-cancel leaves durable state untouched), cancel with reason whitelist {user/operator/shutdown/quota}→`RequestCancellation`, diagnostics health block + bounded support export (≤1 MiB, O_EXCL 0600).
- Files: `internal/app/run_commands.go`, `internal/app/run_usecases.go` (`repositoryRunUseCases`), `internal/runcontrol` observation API.
- Key tests: `TestRunCommandsListShowFollowCancelDiagnosticsAndSupport`, `TestRunFollowReplaysTerminalJournalAndStopsWithoutCancelling`, `TestRunHelpDoesNotOpenRepository` (`run_commands_test.go`).
- Seams: same queries as web SSE and TUI polling; same `RequestCancellation` as all interfaces.
- Risk: normal; it is the operator's window into the S9 durable spine.

### IB1 — `web-routing-projection-compat` (domain B)
- Behaviour: hand-rolled route matcher (~47 page/API/static GETs + mutations): HTML pages (dashboard/projects/project/sprint/studies/study/runs/run/artifact/operation/operation-confirm/QA pages), `/api/v1/*` JSON reads with strict param regexes and query-string allowlist, artifact preview via HMAC opaque refs + symlink-evaluated containment + 256 KiB bound, go:embed templates (primitive→component→layout→page hierarchy validated at startup) and 14-name static allowlist; compatibility frozen by executable fixtures.
- Files: `internal/web/{routes,handlers,artifacts}.go`, `templates/**`, `static/**` (server-side parts), `web_usecases.go` projection layer (`bounded[T]`, honest `meta.returned_count/total_count/truncated`), `api_compatibility_test.go`, `routes_test.go`, `packaging_test.go`.
- Failure semantics: unknown query → 400; `/api/v2/*` → 404; wrong method → 405+Allow; internal causes collapsed to generic codes (`writeRouteError`, tested `routes_test.go:185`).
- Key facts: QA API returns raw app structs verbatim (no DTO layer, `qa_handlers.go`); markdown reaches browser only through goldmark-based `RenderSafeMarkdown` (raw HTML omitted, unsafe links filtered, `markdown.go:11-22`); JSON encoding uses `SetEscapeHTML(true)`; `Cache-Control: no-store` globally except static revalidated assets.
- Seams: consumes dashboardUseCases/webUseCases queries; artifact refs minted in-memory per process (restart invalidates).
- Risk: high — largest read/projection surface; escaping posture and envelope stability are review targets.

### IB2 — `web-operation-hub-sse` (domain B)
- Behaviour: two-phase operations (prepare → confirmation_token TTL 2 min, cap 128 → start consuming token against freshly prepared canonical request+fingerprint, atomic consume, sha256(session‖token) dedup for double-click idempotency); hub caps (MaxActiveOperations=8 → 429+Retry-After, streams 32/subscribers-per-op 8, ring 256 events/256 KiB/op, encoded event cap 16 KiB → warning stub); SSE with closed event-name set {snapshot, progress, warning, finding, artifact, cancel_requested, recovery_required, terminal}, Last-Event-ID replay, `recovery_required` on replay gap, slow-subscriber drop, 30 min lifetime/15 s heartbeat; graceful drain (reject new starts, cancel non-terminal ops reason `server_shutdown`, deadline → persist cleanup-uncertain markers via `RecordOperationCleanupUncertain`, project `cleanup_uncertain` terminal state).
- Files: `internal/web/{operations,operation_handlers,server}.go`, `security.go` preparation store, app glue `durable_operations.go`, `web_usecases.go` (`ReconcileOperations` at startup walks sprints+studies, `web_usecases.go:563-591`).
- Inventory facts: mutations outside the token flow exist — `POST /projects/{p}/sprints/create` (session+CSRF only, direct `CreateSprintWorkspace`, `handlers.go:1314-1334`), `DELETE /api/v1/runs/{id}` and HTML cancels (direct cancel, CSRF-checked); browser JS closes terminal SSE then `window.location.reload()` (`static/app.js:887-894`) while the durable-run timeline path stops without reload; pre-durable `op_*` ids get 410 `legacy_operation_not_retained`.
- Key tests: `operations_test.go` (hub lifecycle/drain/deadline-cleanup-uncertain/ninth-op rejection/redaction-before-retention), `sse_test.go`, `operations_contract_test.go` (browser kind table, SSE frame shape, error-code table), `integration_test.go` (real end-to-end prepare→start→poll).
- Seams: AcceptOperation durable seam; cleanup-uncertainty seam shared with study owner reconciliation.
- Risk: high — this is where user intent becomes durable child work; drain/token/replay semantics deserve deep review.

### IB3 — `web-security-session-origin` (domain B)
- Behaviour: loopback-trust model (no authn): signed anonymous session cookie (`ultraplan_session`, HMAC-SHA256 per-process secret, HttpOnly+SameSite=Strict, MaxAge 3600, no Secure flag — plain HTTP loopback), session-bound deterministic CSRF (constant-time compare on API headers; plain `!=` on `_csrf` form fields — asymmetry fact), Host pinning to listener-resolved numeric loopback authority, Origin tiering (mutations exact-origin or port-stripped-with-fetch-metadata+exact-Referer proofs; reads/SSE lenient-empty-Origin variants; static exempt), bind refusal for anything non-loopback (double validation pre-listen and post-resolve, `serve_commands.go:117-139`, `server.go:43-74`), body/framing discipline (64 KiB bodies on allowlisted routes only, duplicate CL / CL+TE rejection, DisallowUnknownFields JSON), security headers (CSP, nosniff, DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, no CORS anywhere), abuse caps (32 in-flight requests, no per-session op cap), redaction before projection (`safeProjectedText` markers + `[redacted path]` + 4096 bound; tool payloads sanitised upstream in app `captureToolObservation`/`redactObservableValue`; normalized access-log buckets; `safeOperationCause` whitelist).
- Files: `internal/web/{security,server_policy}.go`, middleware attach points in `server.go`/`handlers.go`, `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:45-62` (argv-array browser launch, target always `http://<loopback>/`).
- Inventory facts: `validCommandOrigin` docstring describes port-stripping tolerance that its equality body does not implement — tolerance actually lives one layer up in `validCommandRequestOrigin` (`security.go:269-298`); `validOrigin`/`validOperationReadOrigin` have no production callers; session validity = HMAC validity until process restart (no embedded expiry); no HSTS/COOP/COEP/CORP headers; open-browser failures never fail the server.
- Key tests: `security_test.go` (host/origin matrices, port-strip proof requirements, framing, limits, log normalization, no-CORS), `server_policy_test.go` (fail-closed coherence), `TestPreparationStoreBindingExpiryReplayAndCapacity`, templates_test.go (JS CSRF retry-once).
- Risk: high — everything browser-reachable crosses here; comment/body drift and the form-vs-API comparison asymmetry are exactly where silent control weakening would hide.

### IC1 — `tui-dashboard-navigation-projection` (domain C)
- Behaviour: bubbletea alt-screen dashboard; explicit `Routes` stack with exactly 14 route kinds across Projects/Studies/Runs tabs; typed key map (`keys.go:24-55`); read-only projections from Dashboard/Runs/RunEvents/QA-bounded summaries/artifact previews (allowlist + symlink rejection + 32 KiB cap, `usecases.go:214-242`); glamour markdown rendering with raw fallback; wholesale data replacement on refresh (manual `r`, post-terminal, 1 Hz tick only while a run view is open — no background poller otherwise, so external CLI/web changes appear only via these refreshes).
- Files: `internal/tui/{app,model,views,viewport,theme,markdown}.go`, glue `internal/app/tui_commands.go:21-61`.
- Inventory facts: byte-slicing truncation (`truncateForDisplay` at 300 bytes; `boundContent` at `PreviewByteLimit` bytes) is rune-unaware; wrap-induced extra rows not modeled by line-count viewport; stale-response guards exist only for route-scoped messages (Preview/Validation/Confirmation), not Load/Refresh; `displaySafe` applied to findings/errors but not preview Content.
- Key tests: `views_test.go` (path-leak negatives, markdown engaged, ordering), `viewport_test.go`, `qa_view_test.go` (verdict-neutral rendering forced fail), `model_test.go` navigation/focus.
- Risk: normal — misprojection/truncation class rather than state corruption.

### IC2 — `tui-operation-lifecycle-cancel` (domain C)
- Behaviour: mandatory CONFIRM dialog pipeline (PrepareOperation → rendered Confirmation → Enter → beginOperation computes sha256(CanonicalRequest+NUL+fingerprint) digest → DurableOperationManager.AcceptOperation accept-before-goroutine, Existing dedup message); foreground event stream (128-buffer channel, emit-side non-blocking sends are silently dropped when full; RecordOperationEvent errors other than ErrWebUnavailable also stop forwarding; model keeps last 100 events); quit refused while Running (hides pane, demands `c`); Esc detaches display without cancelling; `c` semantics are overloaded in priority order: active durable op → `runs.CancelRun("user_requested")`; running w/o durable id → local ctx cancel; RouteRun → CancelRun + refresh; else selected study → `beginOperation({OperationStudyCancel})` directly, bypassing PrepareOperation/AcceptOperation because `Confirmation == nil` gates the accept block (`app.go:235,138-139`) — verified by mapper.
- Files: `internal/tui/app.go`, `model.go`, `views.go`, `qa_view.go`; manager `internal/app/durable_operations.go:97-156`.
- Inventory facts: enum kinds `sprint-stage`/`sprint-stage-dry-run` and `validate` are never constructed by any TUI nav item (validate goes straight to `UseCases.Validate` via `validationCmd`, skipping confirm/durability entirely); `OperationStudyStart` appears only in tests/render branches — nav always sends `OperationStudyResume` even for first run (parallelism form default 3, validated 1–64); success message "durable cancellation requested" stored in the Error field (`app.go:127`); no TUI string-vocabulary parity test exists (typed constants only); teaModel-level tests use fakes without DurableOperationManager, so the real accept/stream plumbing is exercised only indirectly via `app/tui_commands_test.go:52`.
- Key tests: `TestOperationConfirmationProgressBoundAndTerminal`, `TestEscapeHidesForegroundRunWithoutCancelling`, `TestCancelKeyWorksInsideRunView`, `TestRunLoopParallelParameterEntry`, `TestDurableRunListDetailUsesCanonicalVocabulary` (+tick re-arm), `TestQAViewUsesVerdictNeutralTextAtNarrowWidth`.
- Seams: shares S9 acceptance/cancellation seams with web; non-TTY chain derives from bubbletea v1.3.10 module cache (`/dev/tty` fallback then exit 1; dependency-source-derived, not executed).
- Risk: normal-high — the confirm/durability bypass paths and silent event drops define what the user believes happened.

### ID1 — `cross-interface-usecase-vocabulary` (domain D)
- Behaviour: the convergence fabric itself: `dashboardUseCases` implements ReadOnlyUseCases+WebOperations(+RunUseCases/DurableOperationManager optional capabilities returning ErrWebUnavailable when nil); `webUseCases` embeds it by value and adds additive capability interfaces (prompt/resources/models/sprint-create/dimensions); `sharedOperationRunner` maps OperationKind → product service calls with OperationEvent emission; closed 27-kind vocabulary pinned to browser strings by `TestBrowserOperationKindContract` and to shipped JS by regex-extracting `static/js/sse.js` stableEvents; cancellation converges on `runcontrol.Repository.RequestCancellation` from all three frontends (reason hard-coded `user_requested` in web/TUI, whitelisted in CLI); observation converges on `repositoryRunUseCases` (identical 512/250ms-1s algorithm in CLI follow and web SSE; TUI polls ≤200 events at 1 Hz instead).
- Files: `internal/app/{operations,usecases,run_usecases,web_usecases,durable_operations,operation_runner,surfaces}.go`; parity pins `internal/web/operations_contract_test.go`, `api_compatibility_test.go`.
- Divergence register (facts): CLI-only — `ultraplan code`, diagnostics/support export, sprint metrics, execute defer, study reset interactive confirm, storage migrate, defaults/skills install; web-only — sprint create, models endpoint, PromptBundle API, timeline API, study resources, roadmap join view, HMAC artifact refs; TUI-only — parallelism form, overloaded `c`; kind asymmetries — CLI never emits `execute-resume` (`--resume` still accepted as `execute-start`, `sprint_commands.go:338`), web form defaults `study_run_loop` → `OperationStudyStart` while CLI/TUI always send resume-kind, `study-cancel` mapped+contract-tested for web but no shipped template/JS issues it; single-stage `FlowStage` reachable only behind the operation layer (no CLI verb); durable acceptance mechanisms differ — CLI `beginDurableCLICommand` synchronous with empty digest (no dedup alias) vs web confirmation-token-derived dedup key vs TUI canonical+fingerprint digest; QA-cancel ownership precheck exists only on the CLI/ad-hoc path (`sprint_usecases.go:716-737`) — generic web/TUI run cancel performs no such target validation; validate/prompt wiring differs per frontend (CLI local switches vs `validateSprintStage`/`promptSprintStage` helpers vs web PromptBundle duplicating the switch again).
- Workspace-contract cross-reference (CURRENT-CONTRACT): `system/contracts/surfaces/cli.md` (stable exit codes, stdout/stderr discipline, destructive-action explicitness, non-interactive determinism) and `api-contracts.md` (versioned schemas, stable error codes, pagination, backpressure) are the applicable anchors reviewers should diff implementation against; `frontend.md` targets a `frontend/src/...` ownership tree that does not exist in this repo (Go-embedded templates/JS instead) — treat as generic template context, HISTORY-like for this target.
- Risk: critical-as-lens — any drift between the three frontends' semantics (kinds, durability, cancellation reasons, classification) produces "same action, different outcome depending on door", which is the costliest interface defect class in this product.

---

## Seam register (interface-specific)

1. **Durable acceptance ×3 mechanisms** — `beginDurableCLICommand` (empty digest, sync) / web `startConfirmed` (token dedup key, transient fallback on ErrWebUnavailable) / TUI `beginOperation` (canonical+fingerprint digest, gated on Confirmation != nil). Same repository.Accept underneath.
2. **Operation-kind vocabulary** — Go enum ↔ browser strings (contract-tested) ↔ TUI typed constants (compile-time only, no exhaustive parity test).
3. **Cancellation** — three doors, one `RequestCancellation`; study-cancel is a separate lock-signal mechanism, not a durable cancellation record.

## 1. Two-phase operation flow (prepare → token → start)

**Prepare (API)** — `internal/web/operation_handlers.go:78-120`
- Draining check first (`:83-86`), strict JSON decode (`:88`), spec mapping (`:92`), then `hub.ops.PrepareOperation` (`:97`).

**Token issuance** — `internal/web/security.go:368-411`
- Record fields: `ID "prep_"+rand`, `Token "confirm_"+rand`, `Session`, `Canonical`, `Fingerprint`, full `Confirmation`, `ExpiresAt = now+PreparationTTL` (`security.go:403-407`).
- **TTL**: `PreparationTTL = 2 * time.Minute` (`internal/web/operations.go:21`).
- **Capacity cap**: `MaxPreparations = 128` (`operations.go:20`); `issue` reaps expired records then returns `errOperationCapacity` when full (`security.go:396-402`) → HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 2` (`operation_handlers.go:803-805`).

**Canonical request & fingerprint (app layer)** — `internal/app/operations.go`
- `PrepareOperation` zeroes caller-supplied fingerprint (`:215`), normalizes/trims/dedups/sorts inputs (`:216`, `:523-539`), validates scope charset (`:541-557`; also web-side `validOptionalIdentifier` → `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, ≤128 bytes — `internal/web/handlers.go:22,1035-1038`, `operation_handlers.go:775-777`).
- **CanonicalRequest** = JSON marshal of the stripped request (`canonicalOperationRequest`, `operations.go:577-584`).
- **InputFingerprint** = SHA-256 over `canonical + "\nruntime=" + ModelSource + "\nscope=" + join(Scope,"\x00")` plus every governed input file/dir content (`ultraplan.yml`, sprint artifacts, QA extras; study files) with symlink rejection and sorted dir walks (`operations.go:344-358, 627-661, 663-718`). Marker format `"sha256:<hex>"` (`:707`).
- Server-issued authority comment on `ExpectedFingerprint`: *"Transport decoders must never accept it from a caller"* (`operations.go:129-133`).

**Caller-supplied fingerprint rejection**
- `decodeStrictJSON` uses `DisallowUnknownFields` + single-value enforcement (`operation_handlers.go:593-608`), so a top-level `fingerprint` key is a 400; pinned in `TestOperationHTTPStrictJSONAndCSRF` (`internal/web/operations_test.go:391-394`).

**Start consumes token** — `operation_handlers.go:132-167`
- Requires non-empty `confirmation_token` (`:142-145`); **freshly re-prepares** the same spec to obtain `current.CanonicalRequest`/`current.InputFingerprint` (`:151-155`), then passes a lazy `confirm()` callback into `hub.startConfirmed` (`:156-158`).
- **Atomicity/freshness binding**: `preparationStore.consume` under one mutex: unknown → `errConfirmationReplayed`; already `Consumed` → replayed; expired → marks consumed + `errConfirmationExpired`; session or canonical mismatch → consumed + `errConfirmationMismatch`; stored fingerprint ≠ current fingerprint → consumed + `errStaleConfirmation`; else consumed and returns confirmation (`security.go:413-437`). Error→HTTP mapping: 409 codes `confirmation_expired|mismatch|replayed|stale_confirmation` (`operation_handlers.go:792-799`; contract table `operations_contract_test.go:186-198`).
- Second execution-time check: `RunOperation` strips `ExpectedFingerprint`, re-prepares, fails with `ErrStaleOperation` *before* invoking any runner if fingerprints diverge (`internal/app/operations.go:376-386`).

**Idempotency / dedup key**
- Web-level key: `confirmationDedupKey(session, token) = hex(sha256(session + "\x00" + token))` (`security.go:448-451`).
- Hub dedup map: replayed start with same key+session returns cloned existing doc instead of a new run (`operations.go:154-159`); key recorded only for live records and dropped on reap (`operations.go:209-211, 565-575`); pinned `operations_test.go:375-384`.

Constants (`internal/web/operations.go:18-32`):
- `MaxActiveOperations = 8` → `errOperationCapacity` on 9th (`:164-167`; test `operations_test.go:209-232`).
- `MaxEventsPerOperation = 256`, `MaxEventBytesPerOperation = 256KiB` ring-buffer eviction loop (`operations.go:450-455`).
- `MaxEncodedEventBytes = 16KiB`: oversized events are replaced by a **warning stub** `{"message":"event projection exceeded the safe size limit"}` renamed to event `warning` (`operations.go:442-448`); marshal failures counted as `projectionDrops` (`:437-441`).
- `MaxSubscribersPerOperation = 8` per op, `MaxConcurrentStreams = 32` hub-wide → `errSubscriberCapacity` (`operations.go:384-387`) → HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 2` (`operation_handlers.go:806-808`). Subscriber queue `SubscriberQueueSize = 32` (`operations.go:28`).

## 4. SSE

**Endpoints**
1. `/api/v1/operations/{id}/events` GET (`routes.go:389-390`) → `handleOperationEvents` (`operation_handlers.go:230-291`): transient-hub stream; falls back to durable polling projection `followDurableOperationEvents` (`:447-514`) when the op isn't in this process's hub.
2. `/api/v1/runs/{id}/events?after=N` GET (`routes.go:393-394`) → `handleRunEvents` (`run_handlers.go:931-1047`): JSON replay unless `Accept: text/event-stream`, then `followRunSSE`.

**Allowed event-name set**: `stableOperationEventName` whitelist `{snapshot, progress, warning, finding, artifact, cancel_requested, recovery_required, terminal}`, everything else coerced to `progress` (`operations.go:470-477`). Frame format `id: %d\nevent: %s\ndata: %s\n\n` (`operation_handlers.go:588-591`). Durable-run mapping of run-event types to these names at `operation_handlers.go:516-534`; durable-run endpoint emits its own single event name `run` (`run_handlers.go:1019`).

**Last-Event-ID replay**: `parseEventID` accepts empty→0 or uint64 decimal, else error (`operations.go:660-669`). `subscribe` replays retained events with `ID > lastID` (`operations.go:397-402`); if `lastID < oldestRetained−1` it appends a **`recovery_required`** event (with oldest/newest retained ids + refresh path) followed by a fresh `snapshot` (`operations.go:388-396`), counter `replayGaps`. Durable fallback rejects `cursor_ahead` (409) and `replay_gap` (409) (`operation_handlers.go:455-461`); run endpoint likewise (`run_handlers.go:968-980`). Client JS never sends Last-Event-ID itself; the durable client uses `?after=` query (`static/app.js:1694`) with preflight replay fetch handling 409 (`app.js:1661-1682`).

**Heartbeat / lifetime**: `SSEHeartbeat = 15s` (`operations.go:30`), emitted as `: heartbeat\n\n` (`operation_handlers.go:265-285, 503-507`); write deadline `now + MaxStreamLifetime + SSEHeartbeat` (`:254`); hard connection lifetime `MaxStreamLifetime = 30min` timer closes the handler (`:267, 285-286`). Response headers `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (`:255-257`). Durable-run poller heartbeats adaptively (250ms/1s poll, heartbeat only when idle timer fires) (`run_handlers.go:1004-1046`).

**Terminal-frame client behaviour (shipped JS)**: on `terminal` event the operations page clears timers, closes the stream, announces state, then **reloads the page** (`window.location.reload()`) — `static/app.js:887-894`. Durable-run page does *not* reload: it stops following and prints "Terminal event committed." (`app.js:1703-1707`). Reconnect-on-error messaging at `app.js:897-904`.

**Subscriber cleanup**: unsubscribe closure guarded by `sync.Once` (`operations.go:412-424`); `finish()` closes/removes all subscribers and decrements streams (`:303-308`); shutdown path does the same (`:550-556`); terminal-state subscribers get an already-closed channel (`:405-411`). Browser side: `pagehide` closes both streams (`app.js:1738-1744`), AbortController wiring `static/js/app.js:1-6` + `UltraPlanSSE.closeOnAbort` (`static/js/sse.js:6-10`).

## 5. Shutdown / drain

- Signals: `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` in `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:19`.
- Serve loop: on ctx cancellation — `ShutdownTimeout = 10s` context, `hub.drainAndWait(shutdownCtx)`, then `cancelOperations()`, then `server.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)`; cleanup error wins over serve errors (`internal/web/server.go:131-153`).
- `drainAndWait` (`operations.go:479-503`): sets `draining=true`; new starts rejected with `errServerDraining` (`operations.go:160-163`) and prepare endpoints refuse up front (`operation_handlers.go:83-86, 298-301`); cancels every non-terminal op with reason `"server_shutdown"` (preserved verbatim by `canonicalCancelReason`, `operations.go:625-632`) emitting `cancel_requested`; waits each `record.done`; on deadline expiry → `persistCleanupUncertain` then `markCleanupUncertain`, returning joined errors.
- **Cleanup-uncertain persistence** (`operations.go:505-531`): per non-terminal op, 1s-budget call to `OperationCleanupRecorder.RecordOperationCleanupUncertain{OperationID, Request, Reason:"server_shutdown", RecordedAt}` → `webUseCases.RecordOperationCleanupUncertain` delegates to sprint/study services (`internal/app/web_usecases.go:540-561`).
- **Marker format/persistence**: sprint `.cleanup-uncertain.json` (`internal/sprint/cleanup_uncertain.go:15,31-57` — schemaVersion 1, operationId, kind, reason must equal `"server_shutdown"`, ownerPid, recordedAt; atomic write); study variant `cleanup-uncertain.json` (`internal/study/cleanup_uncertain.go:15`).
- **In-memory projection**: record forced to state `cleanup_uncertain`, reason `server_shutdown`, terminal event appended, subscribers closed (`operations.go:533-556`).
- **Downstream projection**: reconciliation at startup (`server.go:76-81` → `ReconcileOperations`, `web_usecases.go:563-589`) and mutation-lock acquisition consume the marker: running execute tasks marked failed with diagnostic `recovery-interrupted`, interrupted QA phase set with blocker "the prior QA owner stopped…", marker removed only if changes were made, otherwise `ErrCleanupUncertain` surfaces (`internal/sprint/locks.go:38-110`). `cleanup_uncertain` is a terminal lifecycle everywhere (`operations.go:616-623`; contract test `operations_contract_test.go:108-140`; browser terminal lists include it, `static/app.js:1119,1676`).

## 6. Session model

- Cookie: name `ultraplan_session`, value `<id>.<hex HMAC>`, `Path:/`, `HttpOnly:true`, `SameSite:Lax(StrictMode)`, `MaxAge:3600`; **no `Secure` flag** (plain-http loopback origin) — issuance `security.go:113` whenever no valid cookie present.
- Secret: `[32]byte` from `crypto/rand` per `newSecurityMiddleware` instance (i.e., per-process); deterministic fallback `sha256(authority + now)` only if rand fails (`security.go:96-98`).
- Value construction: `session + "." + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "session:"+session))` (`signSession`, `security.go:228-232`).
- Validation: `readSession` requires exactly two parts with a 32-char id, recomputes MAC, compares whole cookie value with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` (`security.go:234-245`).
- Expiry enforcement location: **browser-side only** — cookie MaxAge; `readSession` contains no time check, and the signed value embeds no timestamp. Server-side lifetime is bounded indirectly by the per-process secret. (Fact stated from code; no additional expiry code exists elsewhere in `internal/web`.)
- Session binding into CSRF: `csrfFor = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "csrf:"+session))` (`security.go:247-251`), computed per-request and placed in ctx (`security.go:115-118`), exposed as response header `X-CSRF-Token` on **every** response (`security.go:116`) and injected into pages via `meta[name=ultraplan-csrf]` (`templates/shell.html:7`; render sets `page.CSRF`, `handlers.go:1130-1131`).

## 7. CSRF

- Derivation: see above (HMAC over session id, domain-separated `"csrf:"` prefix vs cookie's `"session:"` prefix).
- **API comparison (constant-time)** — quoted, `security.go:155-156`:
  ```go
  case (apiOperationMutation || apiRunMutation) && subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(r.Header.Get("X-CSRF-Token")), []byte(csrf)) != 1:
      m.reject(tracked, r, http.StatusForbidden, "csrf_failed", ...)
  ```
- **HTML form comparison (operator `!=`, not constant-time)** — quoted, `operation_handlers.go:294` (identical pattern at `:331`, `:382`; `handlers.go:1315`; `run_handlers.go:890`):
  ```go
  if err := r.ParseForm(); err != nil || r.FormValue("_csrf") != csrfToken(r.Context()) {
      h.renderError(w, r, http.StatusForbidden, "Request rejected", ...)
  ```
- JS retry-once logic: shipped twice (fallback embedded copy + module): on attempt 0, a 403 carrying an `X-CSRF-Token` response header with error code `session_required` or `csrf_failed` adopts the replacement token into the meta tag and retries exactly once — `static/js/operations.js:22-37`; fallback duplicate `static/app.js:684-699`. Token read from `meta[name="ultraplan-csrf"]` (`operations.js:20-21`, `app.js:593`).

## 8. Origin / Host controls

- **Host pinning**: `case r.Host != m.authority:` → 403 `host_rejected` (`security.go:149-150`); authority is the canonical numeric-loopback listener address (`server.go:68-74`; `canonicalAuthority` rejects non-numeric/non-loopback, `server.go:167-177`).
- **Mutations tier**: `validCommandRequestOrigin` (`security.go:280-298`) — exact match OR tolerance where Origin lost its port, requiring: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`; all three of Origin/expected/Referer parse without userinfo; schemes equal; hostnames equal; received port empty AND expected port non-empty; and `refererURL.Scheme+"://"+refererURL.Host == expected` (exact Referer authority proof).
- **Read tier for op status/stream**: `validOperationReadRequestOrigin` = Origin absent OK, else same command logic (`security.go:157-158, 304-306`).
- **Everything else (pages/APIs, non-static)**: `validReadRequestOrigin` — identical body (`security.go:159-160, 312-314`).
- **Static assets**: exempt from all origin checks (`staticAsset` carve-out at `security.go:141,159`); opaque `Origin: null` accepted for static only (test `security_test.go:52-63`).
- Docstring-vs-body notes:
  - `validCommandOrigin` docstring claims it *"permits a browser shell or local reverse proxy to omit or rewrite only the port…"*, but the body is bare equality `return origin == expected` — the port tolerance actually lives in `validCommandRequestOrigin` (`security.go:269-274` vs `280-298`).
  - Dead helpers (zero callers anywhere in repo, verified by grep): `validOrigin` (`security.go:262-267`, tolerates empty origin), `validOperationReadOrigin` (`security.go:300-302`), `eventIDHeader` (`operation_handlers.go:872-880`).
- Tests pinning tiers: exact-command-origin matrix incl. `null`, wrong scheme, different loopback IP (`security_test.go:118-148`); port-stripped mutation allowed only with proofs (`:150-166`) and rejected for missing/cross-site fetch metadata, wrong Referer port, missing Referer (`:198-225`); read-only equivalents (`:168-196`); stream origin tiers (`:227-281`).

- **Body caps**: `MaxBodyBytes = 64KiB` (`security.go:24`); `ContentLength > MaxBodyBytes` → 413 (`security.go:161-162`); bodies on non-allowlisted routes rejected 400 (`hasBody && !operationBody`, `security.go:142-143,163-164`); allowlisted operation routes get `http.MaxBytesReader` (`security.go:166-168`). Per-route body allowlist enumerated at `security.go:143` (prepare/start/cancel/sprint_create/run_cancel).
- **CL/TE**: duplicate `Content-Length` headers, or CL together with `TransferEncoding` → `ambiguousRequestFraming` → 400 (`security.go:147-148,180-183`).
- **DisallowUnknownFields**: `decodeStrictJSON` also enforces `Content-Type: application/json` and exactly one JSON value (`operation_handlers.go:593-608`).
- **In-flight cap**: `MaxInFlight = 32` counting semaphore; exhausted → 503 `unavailable` (`security.go:22,94,121-131`).
- **Access-log normalization**: `normalizedRoute` buckets (dashboard/projects/project_detail/sprint_detail/studies/study_detail/artifact/api_artifact/api_v1/api_unknown/static/not_found) with method/status/duration_ms/response_bytes, no path/query echo (`security.go:174-176,339-366`); redaction pinned by `security_test.go:333-351`.

# Inventory: browser-mutation → durable work → SSE progress → loopback security
Repo: `/tmp/opencode/map05-frozen` @ `f73c4dc` ("chore: update agentwrap terminal output fix"). All paths below are relative to this root. Read-only; nothing modified.

---

## 1. Two-phase operation flow (prepare → token → start)

**Prepare (API)** — `internal/web/operation_handlers.go:78-120`
- Draining check first (`:83-86`), strict JSON decode (`:88`), spec mapping (`:92`), then `hub.ops.PrepareOperation` (`:97`).
- Token issued per-session by `preparationStore.issue` (`:102`); DTO returns `PreparationID`, `Operation`, `AffectedPaths`, `MutationClass`, `Prerequisites`, `InputFingerprint`, `ExpiresAt`, `ConfirmationToken` (`:108-112`). HTML twin at `operation_handlers.go:293-328`.

**Token issuance** — `internal/web/security.go:368-411`
- Record fields: `ID "prep_"+rand`, `Token "confirm_"+rand`, `Session`, `Canonical`, `Fingerprint`, full `Confirmation`, `ExpiresAt = now+PreparationTTL` (`security.go:403-407`).
- **TTL**: `PreparationTTL = 2 * time.Minute` (`internal/web/operations.go:21`).
- **Capacity cap**: `MaxPreparations = 128` (`operations.go:20`); `issue` reaps expired records then returns `errOperationCapacity` when full (`security.go:396-402`) → HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 2` (`operation_handlers.go:803-805`).

**Canonical request & fingerprint (app layer)** — `internal/app/operations.go`
- `PrepareOperation` zeroes caller-supplied fingerprint (`:215`), normalizes/trims/dedups/sorts inputs (`:216`, `:523-539`), validates scope charset (`:541-557`; also web-side `validOptionalIdentifier` → `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, ≤128 bytes — `internal/web/handlers.go:22,1035-1038`, `operation_handlers.go:775-777`).
- **CanonicalRequest** = JSON marshal of the stripped request (`canonicalOperationRequest`, `operations.go:577-584`).
- **InputFingerprint** = SHA-256 over `canonical + "\nruntime=" + ModelSource + "\nscope=" + join(Scope,"\x00")` plus every governed input file/dir content (`ultraplan.yml`, sprint artifacts, QA extras; study files) with symlink rejection and sorted dir walks (`operations.go:344-358, 627-661, 663-718`). Marker format `"sha256:<hex>"` (`:707`).
- Server-issued authority comment on `ExpectedFingerprint`: *"Transport decoders must never accept it from a caller"* (`operations.go:129-133`).

**Caller-supplied fingerprint rejection**
- `decodeStrictJSON` uses `DisallowUnknownFields` + single-value enforcement (`operation_handlers.go:593-608`), so a top-level `fingerprint` key is a 400; pinned in `TestOperationHTTPStrictJSONAndCSRF` (`internal/web/operations_test.go:391-394`).

**Start consumes token** — `operation_handlers.go:132-167`
- Requires non-empty `confirmation_token` (`:142-145`); **freshly re-prepares** the same spec to obtain `current.CanonicalRequest`/`current.InputFingerprint` (`:151-155`), then passes a lazy `confirm()` callback into `hub.startConfirmed` (`:156-158`).
- **Atomicity/freshness binding**: `preparationStore.consume` under one mutex: unknown → `errConfirmationReplayed`; already `Consumed` → replayed; expired → marks consumed + `errConfirmationExpired`; session or canonical mismatch → consumed + `errConfirmationMismatch`; stored fingerprint ≠ current fingerprint → consumed + `errStaleConfirmation`; else consumed and returns confirmation (`security.go:413-437`). Error→HTTP mapping: 409 codes `confirmation_expired|mismatch|replayed|stale_confirmation` (`operation_handlers.go:792-799`; contract table `operations_contract_test.go:186-198`).
- Second execution-time check: `RunOperation` strips `ExpectedFingerprint`, re-prepares, fails with `ErrStaleOperation` *before* invoking any runner if fingerprints diverge (`internal/app/operations.go:376-386`).

**Idempotency / dedup key**
- Web-level key: `confirmationDedupKey(session, token) = hex(sha256(session + "\x00" + token))` (`security.go:448-451`).
- Hub dedup map: replayed start with same key+session returns cloned existing doc instead of a new run (`operations.go:154-159`); key recorded only for live records and dropped on reap (`operations.go:209-211, 565-575`); pinned `operations_test.go:375-384`.
- Durable-level alias: digest passed as `OperationAlias`/`ConfirmationDigest` on run-control `Accept`; on conflict resolves alias and returns `Existing: true` with prior RunID/lifecycle (`internal/app/durable_operations.go:103-112`), cross-manager dedup pinned `durable_operations_test.go:92-124`.

**Legacy op-id handling (410)**
- `legacyOperationID(id) = strings.HasPrefix(id, "op_")` (`operation_handlers.go:422`); API status/cancel/events and HTML status/cancel each return **HTTP 410 Gone**, code `legacy_operation_not_retained` (`:175-178, 215-218, 241-244, 371-374, 398-401`).

**Durable acceptance order** — `operations.go:181-199`: after token consumption, if ops implement `DurableOperationManager`, `AcceptOperation` runs under the hub lock; durable RunID replaces the generated id; `Existing` returns early doc with `RefreshPath "/runs/<id>"`. Execution goroutine then calls `RunOperation` with emit → every app event persisted via `RecordOperationEvent` before broadcast (`operations.go:231-255`), finish persisted via `FinishOperation` with 30s budget (`operations.go:234-241`; impl `durable_operations.go:266-299`).

## 2. Mutations OUTSIDE the prepare/confirm token flow

Middleware classifies five mutation families (`security.go:134-139`):

| Endpoint | Route | Handler | Protections |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sprint create | POST `/projects/{p}/sprints/create` (`routes.go:349-350`) | `handleSprintCreate` writes workspace dirs (`handlers.go:1312-1334`) | valid session required (`security.go:151-152`); exact/port-stripped command origin (`:153-154`); form-field `_csrf` compare (`handlers.go:1315-1318`); slug charset check (`:1325-1327`); body allowed but unused |
| Run cancel (HTML) | POST `/runs/{id}/cancel` (`routes.go:363-364`) | `handleRunPageCancel` → `CancelRun(...,"user_requested")` (`run_handlers.go:889-903`) | session; origin; `_csrf` form compare (`run_handlers.go:890-893`) |
| Operation cancel/start/prepare (HTML) | POST `/operations/*` (`routes.go:325-330,365-366`) | `handleHTMLOperation*` | session; origin; `_csrf` form compare (`operation_handlers.go:294, 331, 382`) |
| Operation cancel (API) | DELETE `/api/v1/operations/{id}` (`routes.go:260-261,387-388`) | `handleOperationCancel` (`operation_handlers.go:206-228`) | session; origin; **constant-time header CSRF** (`security.go:155`) — note: this bypasses prepare/confirm (cancellation needs no token) |
| Run cancel (API) | DELETE `/api/v1/runs/{id}` (`routes.go:264-265,391-392`) | `handleRunCancel` (`run_handlers.go:918-929`) | session; origin; constant-time header CSRF |

All of the above also require Host pinning and pass through the in-flight semaphore. No other mutating routes exist (`allowedMethods`, `routes.go:252-271` — everything else GET/HEAD only). Sprint create additionally has no token/TTL — it's a direct workspace write gated only by the above.

## 3. Operation hub

Constants (`internal/web/operations.go:18-32`):
- `MaxActiveOperations = 8` → `errOperationCapacity` on 9th (`:164-167`; test `operations_test.go:209-232`).
- `MaxEventsPerOperation = 256`, `MaxEventBytesPerOperation = 256KiB` ring-buffer eviction loop (`operations.go:450-455`).
- `MaxEncodedEventBytes = 16KiB`: oversized events are replaced by a **warning stub** `{"message":"event projection exceeded the safe size limit"}` renamed to event `warning` (`operations.go:442-448`); marshal failures counted as `projectionDrops` (`:437-441`).
- `MaxSubscribersPerOperation = 8` per op, `MaxConcurrentStreams = 32` hub-wide → `errSubscriberCapacity` (`operations.go:384-387`) → HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 2` (`operation_handlers.go:806-808`). Subscriber queue `SubscriberQueueSize = 32` (`operations.go:28`).
- **Slow-subscriber policy**: non-blocking send; full queue ⇒ channel closed, subscriber deleted, `slowSubscribers` counter incremented (`operations.go:457-467`; test `operations_test.go:234-268`).
- Terminal result projection: `projectOperationResult` bounds Content to `MaxTerminalResultBytes/2` (128KiB) and whole-DTO overflow drops content/findings and truncates message to 4096 bytes (`operations.go:577-600`); `MaxTerminalResultBytes = 256KiB` (`:25`).
- Retention: terminal records reaped after `TerminalRetention = 10min` on every hub touch (`reapLocked`, `operations.go:565-575`).
- Session ownership: all reads/cancels scoped by `record.session` (`operations.go:315-317, 350, 380-382`); cancel reason canonicalized to `{server_shutdown, timeout, recovery, user_request}` (`operations.go:625-632`).
- Counters struct for starts/active/terminal/capacityRejections/cancellations/activeStreams/slowSubscribers/replayGaps/projectionDrops/shutdownCleanups (`operations.go:120-131`).

## 4. SSE

**Endpoints**
1. `/api/v1/operations/{id}/events` GET (`routes.go:389-390`) → `handleOperationEvents` (`operation_handlers.go:230-291`): transient-hub stream; falls back to durable polling projection `followDurableOperationEvents` (`:447-514`) when the op isn't in this process's hub.
2. `/api/v1/runs/{id}/events?after=N` GET (`routes.go:393-394`) → `handleRunEvents` (`run_handlers.go:931-1047`): JSON replay unless `Accept: text/event-stream`, then `followRunSSE`.

**Allowed event-name set**: `stableOperationEventName` whitelist `{snapshot, progress, warning, finding, artifact, cancel_requested, recovery_required, terminal}`, everything else coerced to `progress` (`operations.go:470-477`). Frame format `id: %d\nevent: %s\ndata: %s\n\n` (`operation_handlers.go:588-591`). Durable-run mapping of run-event types to these names at `operation_handlers.go:516-534`; durable-run endpoint emits its own single event name `run` (`run_handlers.go:1019`).

**Last-Event-ID replay**: `parseEventID` accepts empty→0 or uint64 decimal, else error (`operations.go:660-669`). `subscribe` replays retained events with `ID > lastID` (`operations.go:397-402`); if `lastID < oldestRetained−1` it appends a **`recovery_required`** event (with oldest/newest retained ids + refresh path) followed by a fresh `snapshot` (`operations.go:388-396`), counter `replayGaps`. Durable fallback rejects `cursor_ahead` (409) and `replay_gap` (409) (`operation_handlers.go:455-461`); run endpoint likewise (`run_handlers.go:968-980`). Client JS never sends Last-Event-ID itself; the durable client uses `?after=` query (`static/app.js:1694`) with preflight replay fetch handling 409 (`app.js:1661-1682`).

**Heartbeat / lifetime**: `SSEHeartbeat = 15s` (`operations.go:30`), emitted as `: heartbeat\n\n` (`operation_handlers.go:265-285, 503-507`); write deadline `now + MaxStreamLifetime + SSEHeartbeat` (`:254`); hard connection lifetime `MaxStreamLifetime = 30min` timer closes the handler (`:267, 285-286`). Response headers `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (`:255-257`). Durable-run poller heartbeats adaptively (250ms/1s poll, heartbeat only when idle timer fires) (`run_handlers.go:1004-1046`).

**Terminal-frame client behaviour (shipped JS)**: on `terminal` event the operations page clears timers, closes the stream, announces state, then **reloads the page** (`window.location.reload()`) — `static/app.js:887-894`. Durable-run page does *not* reload: it stops following and prints "Terminal event committed." (`app.js:1703-1707`). Reconnect-on-error messaging at `app.js:897-904`.

**Subscriber cleanup**: unsubscribe closure guarded by `sync.Once` (`operations.go:412-424`); `finish()` closes/removes all subscribers and decrements streams (`:303-308`); shutdown path does the same (`:550-556`); terminal-state subscribers get an already-closed channel (`:405-411`). Browser side: `pagehide` closes both streams (`app.js:1738-1744`), AbortController wiring `static/js/app.js:1-6` + `UltraPlanSSE.closeOnAbort` (`static/js/sse.js:6-10`).

## 5. Shutdown / drain

- Signals: `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` in `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:19`.
- Serve loop: on ctx cancellation — `ShutdownTimeout = 10s` context, `hub.drainAndWait(shutdownCtx)`, then `cancelOperations()`, then `server.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)`; cleanup error wins over serve errors (`internal/web/server.go:131-153`).
- `drainAndWait` (`operations.go:479-503`): sets `draining=true`; new starts rejected with `errServerDraining` (`operations.go:160-163`) and prepare endpoints refuse up front (`operation_handlers.go:83-86, 298-301`); cancels every non-terminal op with reason `"server_shutdown"` (preserved verbatim by `canonicalCancelReason`, `operations.go:625-632`) emitting `cancel_requested`; waits each `record.done`; on deadline expiry → `persistCleanupUncertain` then `markCleanupUncertain`, returning joined errors.
- **Cleanup-uncertain persistence** (`operations.go:505-531`): per non-terminal op, 1s-budget call to `OperationCleanupRecorder.RecordOperationCleanupUncertain{OperationID, Request, Reason:"server_shutdown", RecordedAt}` → `webUseCases.RecordOperationCleanupUncertain` delegates to sprint/study services (`internal/app/web_usecases.go:540-561`).
- **Marker format/persistence**: sprint `.cleanup-uncertain.json` (`internal/sprint/cleanup_uncertain.go:15,31-57` — schemaVersion 1, operationId, kind, reason must equal `"server_shutdown"`, ownerPid, recordedAt; atomic write); study variant `cleanup-uncertain.json` (`internal/study/cleanup_uncertain.go:15`).
- **In-memory projection**: record forced to state `cleanup_uncertain`, reason `server_shutdown`, terminal event appended, subscribers closed (`operations.go:533-556`).
- **Downstream projection**: reconciliation at startup (`server.go:76-81` → `ReconcileOperations`, `web_usecases.go:563-589`) and mutation-lock acquisition consume the marker: running execute tasks marked failed with diagnostic `recovery-interrupted`, interrupted QA phase set with blocker "the prior QA owner stopped…", marker removed only if changes were made, otherwise `ErrCleanupUncertain` surfaces (`internal/sprint/locks.go:38-110`). `cleanup_uncertain` is a terminal lifecycle everywhere (`operations.go:616-623`; contract test `operations_contract_test.go:108-140`; browser terminal lists include it, `static/app.js:1119,1676`).

## 6. Session model

- Cookie: name `ultraplan_session`, value `<id>.<hex HMAC>`, `Path:/`, `HttpOnly:true`, `SameSite:Lax(StrictMode)`, `MaxAge:3600`; **no `Secure` flag** (plain-http loopback origin) — issuance `security.go:113` whenever no valid cookie present.
- Secret: `[32]byte` from `crypto/rand` per `newSecurityMiddleware` instance (i.e., per-process); deterministic fallback `sha256(authority + now)` only if rand fails (`security.go:96-98`).
- Value construction: `session + "." + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "session:"+session))` (`signSession`, `security.go:228-232`).
- Validation: `readSession` requires exactly two parts with a 32-char id, recomputes MAC, compares whole cookie value with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` (`security.go:234-245`).
- Expiry enforcement location: **browser-side only** — cookie MaxAge; `readSession` contains no time check, and the signed value embeds no timestamp. Server-side lifetime is bounded indirectly by the per-process secret. (Fact stated from code; no additional expiry code exists elsewhere in `internal/web`.)

  ```go

  ```
- JS retry-once logic: shipped twice (fallback embedded copy + module): on attempt 0, a 403 carrying an `X-CSRF-Token` response header with error code `session_required` or `csrf_failed` adopts the replacement token into the meta tag and retries exactly once — `static/js/operations.js:22-37`; fallback duplicate `static/app.js:684-699`. ## 6. Argument parsing styles

Five distinct styles:
1. **stdlib `flag` FlagSet** (`ContinueOnError`, output discarded): `run list/show/follow/cancel/diagnostics` (run_commands.go:62-63,106-107,132-134,198-199,231-232) and `serve` (serve_commands.go:19-23, output→stderr). Consequence: parsing stops at first positional, hence…
2. **Custom reorderer `orderRunArgs`** (run_commands.go:463-481): partitions args into flags-vs-positionals so `run show --json <id>` works; recognizes only `--json`,`-h`,`--help` plus value-taking flags passed in the `valued` map (`--after` for follow, `--reason` for cancel); handles `flag=value` (SplitN on "=" :468) and skips the next token for valued flags without "=" (:475-478). Any other dashed token becomes a positional (usage error downstream).
3. **Hand-rolled index loops** — the majority: init-workspace (workspace_commands.go:13-29), defaults (defaults_commands.go:32-50), skills (skills_commands.go:34-59), code (code_commands.go:80-108), study parsers (study_commands.go:241-275, :579-642, :961-988, :1375-1398, :1489-1525), sprint parsers (sprint_commands.go:588-640, :825-877, :1003-1074, :1076-1117, :1119-1191, :1193-1233), config/storage/health linear scans (config_commands.go:22-32; storage_commands.go:42-54; health_commands.go:32-42).
4. **Global pre-parser** `parseGlobalFlags` (app.go:198-220) — extracts `--workspace` from any position, both `--workspace X` and `--workspace=X`.
5. **Positional-grammar switches** with no flag layer at all: project (project_commands.go:37-74), study top-level dispatch (study_commands.go:45-119), sprint `<project> <sprint> <verb>` positional prefix (sprint_commands.go:71-89), including in-band help detection by inspecting `args[k]=="--help"` at fixed depths (project_commands.go:14-31; sprint_commands.go:32-70).

Quirks observed:
- `flag=value` support is inconsistent: supported for `--workspace` (global), `--output`, `--dimension`, `--source`, `--parallel`, `--model` (study), `--stage-model/--stage-variant` (inline double-`=`), and anything via stdlib flag/orderRunArgs; **not** supported for sprint `--to`, `--task`, `--shard`, `--run`, `--level/--suite/--test/--timeout/--override-reason`, `--focus`, `--defer` (would hit "unsupported argument").

- `--workspace=-foo` is accepted (no dash check after `=`, app.go:210-214).
- Sprint `status` accepts `--json` only as the literal last token with exact arity (sprint_commands.go:91-93); `--json --help`-style orders fail as usage errors, unlike `helpRequested` scanning used by the `run` family (run_commands.go:444-451).

## 7. Durable side effects

**`beginDurableCLICommand`** (durable_operations.go:49-60) opens/uses the workspace run-control repository and calls `AcceptOperation(ctx, Confirmation{Request}, "")` — note the **digest is always the empty string from the CLI** (:55). Stored record: runcontrol row with `Target{Kind:"operation", Operation:<kind>, Project/Sprint/Study/Stage/Task}` and `ProductStatus:"prepared"`, `ConfirmationDigest: ""` (durable_operations.go:99-105); kinds are `sprint-flow, verify-start, execute-start, review-start, smoke-start, qa-start, qa-resume, study-start, study-resume` (operations.go:79-100). A lifecycle-running event is appended (:121-129); an owner claim + fencing token is taken (:116-120); heartbeat/cancellation/reconcile loop runs until `finishDurableCLICommand` proposes a terminal outcome (durable_operations.go:71-91, :266-300; finish maps context/deadline/err to TerminalCancelled/TimedOut/Failed/Succeeded :286-297).

**Dedup**: exists in `AcceptOperation` but only when `digest != ""` — on Accept conflict it resolves `ResolveOperationAlias(digest)` and returns `Existing:true` with the prior RunID (durable_operations.go:106-112). Since the CLI always passes `""`, **every CLI invocation creates a new durable run; CLI invocations are never deduplicated**. The dedup path is exercised by `TestDurableOperationDeduplicatesAcrossManagersAndFailsClosed` using explicit digests (durable_operations_test.go:92-115). **Second durable path**: runtime-backed services wrap their runtime in `controlledRuntime` whose `StartRun` independently Accepts/Claims a durable run per runtime call and persists every event + terminal outcome (run_control.go:159-343; terminalOutcome classifier :765-777).

## 4. Durable acceptance mechanisms compared

All three converge on **the same** `durableOperationManager.AcceptOperation` → `runcontrol.Repository.Accept` underneath:

- Shared body: builds `runcontrol.Target{Kind:"operation", Operation:string(req.Kind), Project/Sprint/Study/Stage/Task}` and calls `m.repository.Accept(ctx, Acceptance{Target, ProductStatus:"prepared", OperationAlias: digest, ConfirmationDigest: digest})` (durable_operations.go:97-105); on conflict with non-empty digest resolves `ResolveOperationAlias(digest)` and returns `Existing:true` (:106-112); then `Claim` (:116), fencing token (:120), lifecycle-running event with terminal-compensation proposal on failure (:121-129), child ctx = `context.WithCancel(runcontrol.WithParentRun(ctx, snapshot.RunID))` carrying `durableOperationOwnership` (:130-137). Repository interface: `Accept`, `ResolveOperationAlias` (runcontrol/interfaces.go:50-51).

Per-surface chains:
- **CLI** `beginDurableCLICommand(deps, request)` (durable_operations.go:49-60): digest = **empty string** (`AcceptOperation(deps.ctx, Confirmation{Request: request}, ""` , :55) → **no dedup alias**, no prepare/fingerprint step; synchronous acceptance then synchronous execution with `durable.Context()`; `Finish(runErr)` maps ctx/runErr → Complete/Cancelled/Failed and proposes terminal under a 30s background ctx (:71-84); joined via `finishDurableCLICommand` (:86-91). Call sites: 6× sprint_commands.go (237, 292, 338, 419, 483, 539), 4× study_commands.go (211, 555, 814, 843).
- **Web** `handleOperationStart`/`handleHTMLOperationStart` → `h.hub.startConfirmed(sessionID, confirmationDedupKey(session, token), confirm)` (web/operation_handlers.go:156, 351). Dedup key source: `sha256(session + "\x00" + confirmation_token)` hex (web/security.go:448-451); token itself validated session/canonical/fingerprint-bound and single-use in `preparations.consume` (security.go:420-437). Hub `startConfirmed` (web/operations.go:150-219): dedup map hit returns existing doc (:154-159); capacity/drain gates (:160-167); type-asserts `app.DurableOperationManager` and passes the dedup key **as the digest** to `AcceptOperation` (:181-182); on `ErrWebUnavailable` falls back to an ephemeral in-memory record with `op_` id (:184-199); on `Existing` returns doc with `/runs/{id}` refresh path (:193-197). Events recorded through `manager.RecordOperationEvent`, dropped if not committed (:245-255); `FinishOperation` under 30s ctx (:234-241).
- **TUI** `beginOperation` (tui/app.go:232-269): gated on `manager, ok := m.model.UseCases.(app.DurableOperationManager); ok && m.model.Confirmation != nil` (:235); digest formula = `sha256(Confirmation.CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + Confirmation.InputFingerprint)` hex-encoded (:236-238); `Existing` short-circuits with "matching durable operation already exists" (:245-250); accepted ctx replaces local ctx (:252-254). If the gate fails (e.g. plain `NewOperationalUseCases`, operations.go:872), it runs undurable with a purely local cancel. Event recording + finish mirror the web hub (:286-310).

Digest asymmetry is structural: CLI `""` (per-invocation unique runs), TUI content-derived (re-click of same prepared confirmation dedups), web session-token-derived (double-submit dedup within one browser session).

## 6. Observation convergence

Three algorithms, two constant sets:

- **CLI `run follow`** (run_commands.go:131-195): `repository.Events(after, 512)` batch; re-Snapshot each cycle; exit when `snapshot.Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence` (:180); wait `1s`, dropping to `250ms` when `len(events)==512 || after < LastSequence` (:183-186); ctx.Done stops observation only ("never changes the durable run", :189-191).
- **Web run SSE replay** `followRunSSE` (web/run_handlers.go:993-1046): identical algorithm — batch `512` (:1010), terminal exit rule (:1029-1031), waits `1s`/`250ms` (:1032-1035) — plus heartbeat comment frames; cursor guards `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` vs `OldestRetainedSequence` (:968-980). The **durable-operation SSE fallback** `followDurableOperationEvents` is the same loop projecting run events into operation event names (`durableOperationEvent`, operation_handlers.go:444-534) with wait logic at :498-501. Ephemeral-hub replay is bounded ring buffer instead: `MaxEventsPerOperation=256`, `MaxEncodedEventBytes=16KiB`, `SSEHeartbeat=15s`, `MaxStreamLifetime=30m`, `TerminalRetention=10m` (web/operations.go:18-32, 428-468).
- **TUI polling**: 1-second tick `runViewTickCmd` rescheduled while a run route/view is open (tui/app.go:222-226, 271-273); each refresh queries `Runs(Query{Limit:200})` (:366) and, on a run route, `RunEvents(after = OldestRetainedSequence-1, limit 200)` (:377-381); client-side dedupe by `RunID:sequence` keeping last 200 (model.go:342-357); live operation event channel capped 100 events (model.go:227-229,236-239), delivery channel cap 128 (tui/app.go:266).

Shared queries: all three ultimately read the same `runcontrol.Repository` — CLI via `runRepository` handle (run_commands.go:42-59), TUI/web via `repositoryRunUseCases` (run_usecases.go:37-56) wired at tui_commands.go:51 and serve_commands.go:80.

## 3. sharedOperationRunner

Single runtime-backed implementation "used by terminal and browser adapters" (operation_runner.go:15-18). Kind→service mapping:

Non-runtime kinds are handled earlier in `dashboardUseCases.RunOperation` (operations.go:376-521), which re-prepares, checks fingerprint staleness (`expected != prepared.InputFingerprint → ErrStaleOperation`, :383-385), emits `OperationRunning` (:390), and falls through to `u.runner` for runtime kinds (:513-517).

Event emission points: per-kind Progress callbacks emit `OperationEvent{State: OperationRunning,...}` — flow/stage (:27-30, 41-44), review (:69-71), smoke (:85-87), verify (:106-109), QA (:124-126), study task stats incl. tokens/cost (:139-147); all runtime services additionally stream via `tuiSprintRuntimeProgress(emit)` observer injected by `sprintRuntimeService` (:23,37,54,65,98,119; defined tui_commands.go:63-73); terminal `emit({State: OperationComplete...})` at :166.

Error wrapping/classification: every branch returns `failedOperation(result, e)` (operations.go:751-796) which maps `context.Canceled→cancelled`, smoke/QA/project/sprint typed errors, malformed-state errors → codes like `workflow.cancelled`, `validation.reference`, `workflow.locked`, with Retryable flags; result state set to `OperationCancelled|OperationFailed` (:751-756).

Timeouts/cancellation propagation: caller ctx flows into every service call; `req.Timeout` parsed only for smoke-start (:81-84) and verify-start (:102-105), with parse errors silently discarded (`timeout, _ = time.ParseDuration`); cancellation is cooperative via ctx plus the durable control loop (see §4/§5). QA fence heartbeat uses `context.WithoutCancel` + 30s timeout so cleanup outlives cancellation (durable_operations.go:150-153).

---

## 4. Durable acceptance mechanisms compared

All three converge on **the same** `durableOperationManager.AcceptOperation` → `runcontrol.Repository.Accept` underneath:

- Shared body: builds `runcontrol.Target{Kind:"operation", Operation:string(req.Kind), Project/Sprint/Study/Stage/Task}` and calls `m.repository.Accept(ctx, Acceptance{Target, ProductStatus:"prepared", OperationAlias: digest, ConfirmationDigest: digest})` (durable_operations.go:97-105); on conflict with non-empty digest resolves `ResolveOperationAlias(digest)` and returns `Existing:true` (:106-112); then `Claim` (:116), fencing token (:120), lifecycle-running event with terminal-compensation proposal on failure (:121-129), child ctx = `context.WithCancel(runcontrol.WithParentRun(ctx, snapshot.RunID))` carrying `durableOperationOwnership` (:130-137). Repository interface: `Accept`, `ResolveOperationAlias` (runcontrol/interfaces.go:50-51).

Per-surface chains:
- **CLI** `beginDurableCLICommand(deps, request)` (durable_operations.go:49-60): digest = **empty string** (`AcceptOperation(deps.ctx, Confirmation{Request: request}, ""` , :55) → **no dedup alias**, no prepare/fingerprint step; synchronous acceptance then synchronous execution with `durable.Context()`; `Finish(runErr)` maps ctx/runErr → Complete/Cancelled/Failed and proposes terminal under a 30s background ctx (:71-84); joined via `finishDurableCLICommand` (:86-91). Call sites: 6× sprint_commands.go (237, 292, 338, 419, 483, 539), 4× study_commands.go (211, 555, 814, 843).
- **Web** `handleOperationStart`/`handleHTMLOperationStart` → `h.hub.startConfirmed(sessionID, confirmationDedupKey(session, token), confirm)` (web/operation_handlers.go:156, 351). Dedup key source: `sha256(session + "\x00" + confirmation_token)` hex (web/security.go:448-451); token itself validated session/canonical/fingerprint-bound and single-use in `preparations.consume` (security.go:420-437). Hub `startConfirmed` (web/operations.go:150-219): dedup map hit returns existing doc (:154-159); capacity/drain gates (:160-167); type-asserts `app.DurableOperationManager` and passes the dedup key **as the digest** to `AcceptOperation` (:181-182); on `ErrWebUnavailable` falls back to an ephemeral in-memory record with `op_` id (:184-199); on `Existing` returns doc with `/runs/{id}` refresh path (:193-197). Events recorded through `manager.RecordOperationEvent`, dropped if not committed (:245-255); `FinishOperation` under 30s ctx (:234-241).
- **TUI** `beginOperation` (tui/app.go:232-269): gated on `manager, ok := m.model.UseCases.(app.DurableOperationManager); ok && m.model.Confirmation != nil` (:235); digest formula = `sha256(Confirmation.CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + Confirmation.InputFingerprint)` hex-encoded (:236-238); `Existing` short-circuits with "matching durable operation already exists" (:245-250); accepted ctx replaces local ctx (:252-254). If the gate fails (e.g. plain `NewOperationalUseCases`, operations.go:872), it runs undurable with a purely local cancel. Event recording + finish mirror the web hub (:286-310).

Digest asymmetry is structural: CLI `""` (per-invocation unique runs), TUI content-derived (re-click of same prepared confirmation dedups), web session-token-derived (double-submit dedup within one browser session).

---

## 5. Cancellation convergence

Every path to `runcontrol.Repository.RequestCancellation` (interfaces.go:57; impl lifecycle.go:70):

- **CLI**: `ultraplan run cancel <id> --reason <r>` → `repository.RequestCancellation` directly (run_commands.go:216); reason flag default `"user_requested"` (:201), allowlist `{user_requested, operator_requested, shutdown_requested, quota_exceeded}` (:394-401).
- **CLI (QA)**: `sprint … qa cancel --run <id>` → `dashboardUseCases.CancelQA` → validates target ownership then `u.runs.CancelRun(ctx, runID, "read-only QA cancellation requested")` (sprint_usecases.go:716-737).
- **TUI**: `c` key while running with ActiveRunID → `runs.CancelRun(m.ctx, RunID(ActiveRunID), "user_requested")` (tui/app.go:109-116); `c` on a RouteRun → same call with `"user_requested"` (:122-131); otherwise falls back to local `m.cancel()` (ctx cancel only, :118-121).
- **Web API**: `DELETE /api/v1/operations/{id}` / POST HTML cancel → hub `cancelOperation(session, id, "user_request")` first (operation_handlers.go:207, 390), falling back to `h.runs.CancelRun(ctx, id, "user_requested")` (:209, 392). Run-page cancels: `h.runs.CancelRun(..., "user_requested")` (run_handlers.go:898 HTML, :923 API). Server drain: `cancelOperation("", id, "server_shutdown")` (web/operations.go:490); canonical reasons limited to `{server_shutdown, timeout, recovery, else user_request}` (operations.go:625-632).

The durable owner side: `controlOperation` ticker polls `Snapshot`, on `CancellationRequested` calls `AcknowledgeCancellation` and cancels the operation ctx (durable_operations.go:223-264).

**Separate mechanism — study-cancel** (does *not* go through RequestCancellation): `sharedOperationRunner case OperationStudyCancel` → `study.CancelRunLoop(listing.Study)` (operation_runner.go:152-162). Implementation: reads `studies/<n>/.ultraplan/run-state.json/../run-loop.lock`, verifies liveness via `syscall.Kill(pid,0)`, refuses foreign-study locks and self-signalling, then sends **SIGINT** to the owner PID (study/locks.go:141-159). Issued by: TUI `c` key on a study view (`beginOperation(OperationStudyCancel)` tui/app.go:132-141) and by any client that posts web kind `study-cancel` (accepted in mapOperationRequest but **no template issues it**). CLI has no `study cancel` command (dispatcher study_commands.go:45-80 has none) — CLI cancels studies via `run cancel` or `--force-unlock` (locks.go:161-167; cli-reference.md:210).

---

## 6. Observation convergence

Three algorithms, two constant sets:

- **CLI `run follow`** (run_commands.go:131-195): `repository.Events(after, 512)` batch; re-Snapshot each cycle; exit when `snapshot.Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence` (:180); wait `1s`, dropping to `250ms` when `len(events)==512 || after < LastSequence` (:183-186); ctx.Done stops observation only ("never changes the durable run", :189-191).

reasoning_details.text:
Peer maps cover trust boundaries (S1-S12) and test topology. My map is interface-lens focused; overlaps: S11 web-http-boundary, S12 tui-console-entry, S2 durable-operation-gateway — I should cross-reference those in seams. Good.

Now compose the final map. Structure per contract:
- Provenance (pinned clone, frozen commit, method, baseline)
- Interface topology paragraph
- Candidate surfaces with domain grouping, behaviour, files/symbols, failure semantics, key tests, seams, risk
- Seam register
- Reviewer prioritisation
- Neutral inventory facts

Surfaces (my own grouping, informed but independent):

Domain A — CLI shell:
- A1 `cli-dispatch-exit-contract` — dispatch, global flags, exit codes, output envelopes, parser styles, help/docs drift.
- A2 `cli-durable-command-acceptance` — beginDurableCLICommand, empty digest, inventory test, interactive prompts, read-only vs mutating classification.

Actually the old stale map had IA1/IA2 similar. My independent pass converged on similar structure — that's fine, it's evidence of stability. But let me structure by my own discovery:

A — CLI shell
  A1 cli-dispatch-exit-contract
  A2 run-cli-observation-control (run list/show/follow/cancel/diagnostics)
  A3 cli-durable-mutation-pipeline? Hmm — durable acceptance for sprint/study CLI commands crosses into ID convergence. Better: keep A1+A2, put acceptance mechanisms into D (cross-interface) where they belong as comparison. But the CLI-specific facts (empty digest, prompts, sniffing) live in A1/A2 and D.

Let me define surfaces:

**A. CLI shell**
- A1 `cli-dispatch-exit-contract`: argv→verb dispatch, exit codes 0–8, envelope/raw/ad-hoc JSON outputs, five parser styles, docs drift, error-text sniffing, interactive prompts on non-TTY.
- A2 `run-cli-observation-control`: run list/show/follow/cancel/diagnostics; reason whitelist; follow algorithm; diagnostics export bounds.

**B. Web console**
- B1 `web-routing-projection-compat`: route table, param/query validation, envelopes/meta, templates/static embed, artifact preview HMAC+containment, markdown pipeline, compat fixtures.
- B2 `web-operation-hub-sse`: two-phase token flow, hub caps, SSE replay/recovery, drain/cleanup-uncertain, out-of-token-flow mutations (sprint create).
- B3 `web-security-session-origin`: loopback trust, session cookie, CSRF asymmetry, origin tiers + docstring/body drift, transport discipline, redaction layers, browser launch.

**C. TUI**
- C1 `tui-dashboard-navigation-projection`: routes/tabs/keys, refresh cadence, truncation/markdown/preview, staleness guards.
- C2 `tui-operation-lifecycle-cancel`: confirm pipeline, digest formula, gating bypass, cancel decision tree, event drops, message storage.

**D. Cross-interface**
- D1 `cross-interface-usecase-vocabulary`: capability interfaces, 27-kind enum + construction matrix, three acceptance mechanisms, cancellation convergence + study-cancel side channel, observation algorithm triplication, workspace resolution single root, divergence register, parity-test absences.

That's 8 surfaces. Each needs: entrypoints, state, dependencies, outputs, failure semantics, primary files/symbols/tests, risk.

Seam register:
1. Durable acceptance ×3 mechanisms → repository.Accept (map-02's S9/S2 territory)
2. Operation-kind vocabulary Go↔browser↔TUI
3. Cancellation: three doors + study-cancel SIGINT side channel
4. Observation: one repo, three formats/algorithms
5. Workspace resolution single discoverWorkspace
6. Redaction layering before human eyes
7. Confirmation authority (fingerprint server-issued)
8. Cleanup uncertainty (drain markers ↔ reconciliation)

Risk rationale ordering: D1 (same-action-different-semantics), B2 (intent→durable work), B3 (security controls), C2 (confirm bypass/silent drops), A1 (exit-code/JSON contract), B1/C1/A2.

Also carry neutral inventory facts. Include provenance noting prior stale map replaced.

Length: aim compact but complete — this goes to the arbiter. The stale map was ~116 lines; mine can be similar or slightly tighter. Write to review/maps/map-05-interface-surfaces.md.

Also per peer convention, write attempt result? Map-02's harness wrote jobs/.../result.md from the final message. The maps/*.md file was written by the agent. I'll write the maps file only, then my final message summarizes.

One more check — verify a couple of remaining claims I haven't personally verified but will assert in the map:
- "serve default listen 127.0.0.1:8080" (worker W1 said serve_commands.go:16) — verified indirectly by two workers consistently. Fine.
- TUI width fixed 100 (tui_commands.go:57). Two workers agree.
- MaxIdentifierBytes etc. — consistent across workers.

## Interface topology in one paragraph

## Seam register (interface-specific)

1. **Durable acceptance ×3 mechanisms** — `beginDurableCLICommand` (empty digest, sync, no dedup) / web `startConfirmed` (token-derived dedup key, ErrWebUnavailable ephemeral fallback) / TUI `beginOperation` (canonical+fingerprint digest, gated on `Confirmation != nil`). Same `repository.Accept` underneath; connects to map-02's S2/S9.
2. **Operation-kind vocabulary** — Go enum ↔ browser aliases (contract-tested) ↔ TUI typed constants (compile-time only) ↔ CLI durable Target kinds (inventory-scanned, not value-checked).
3. **Cancellation** — three doors into `RequestCancellation` with differing reason vocabularies and target validation; `study-cancel` SIGINT side channel bypasses the durable record entirely.
4. **Observation** — one repository; three projections (text/envelope NDJSON, {data,meta}+SSE, rendered TUI); replay constants triplicated; omissions/gaps surfaced differently per door.
5. **Workspace resolution** — single `discoverWorkspace` for all doors; `init-workspace`/`defaults`/`skills` bypass it; serve freezes identity at boot.
6. **Confirmation authority** — fingerprint is server-issued (caller-supplied values zeroed, rejected at decode, re-checked at execution); TUI/web honour it; CLI has no fingerprint concept at all.
7. **Redaction layers before human eyes** — config.RedactValue (CLI/TUI display), safeProjectedText (web hub), redactObservableValue (tool payloads upstream), safeOperationCause (error gating): four layers, different marker sets and bounds.
8. **Cleanup uncertainty** — web drain persists markers after 10 s deadline; study/sprint owners reconcile fail-closed at next boot/lock; CLI interrupt paths write equivalent markers (map-02 overlap).

1. **D1** cross-interface divergence — same-action-different-semantics class: acceptance digests/dedup asymmetry, readOnly write-on-refresh split, QA-precheck gap, unpinned enum literals.

5. **A1** CLI contract — exit-code text-sniffing inconsistencies, parser quirks, undocumented automation surface, prompt-on-non-TTY exits.
6. **B1/C1/A2** — normal-high: projection honesty (unfrozen raw DTOs, restart-invalidated refs, rune-unaware truncation, staleness windows, triplicated replay logic).
